dispositions.justification: Retains the post-baseline shared-contract update. Global accent, font and padding remain separate from table fills; the new header colors do not expand global style keys or bypass inspection and commit checks.

Retains the changed shared-contract closure. Exact field and label targets, typography restrictions and protected bindings remain enforced; table-wide header colors use the separate items-only operation.

Retains the changed shared-contract closure. Original section slots, identifier and dimension constraints, available bindings and protected source identities remain checked; neither batch grants additional field-creation authority.

Retains the changed shared-contract closure. Removal still requires an existing field, original protected bindings remain checked across subsequent edits, and bound-field removal stays outside automatic application.

Retains the changed shared-contract closure. Reordering still requires the complete unique current identity set in an original section, and selected-scope enforcement remains independent of visible step history.
Retains the changed shared-contract closure. Section properties and non-items grid restrictions remain closed; header-row colors belong to set_table_style rather than an expanded section patch.
Retains the changed shared-contract closure. The exact five-section permutation and repeating-header ordering requirement remain documented and validated; the batches do not add section targets.

Retains the changed shared-contract closure. Supported media, bounded margins, custom dimensions and user-supplied printer constraints remain separate from table styling; page operations still require manual application.
Retains the changed shared-contract closure. Logo changes still require an existing asset descriptor or null; table colors and retained tool steps grant no asset creation or disclosure authority.

Retains the changed shared-contract closure. Collection selection remains limited to available absolute array paths with protected-binding checks; additional collections remain human-only and automatic application remains excluded.
Retains the changed shared-contract closure. Heading edits remain stored-text-only and cannot enable the header or widen heading-only scope; visible tool history does not change those semantics.

Adds independent items-only headerBackground and headerColor alongside rowBackground. Closed schemas and the shared service accept six-digit hex or null; inspector, context, history and scoped CSS are updated without widening selected-column authority.

Retains the changed shared-contract closure. Heading and page-number typography targets, bounded values and override clearing remain distinct from table header colors and do not gain cross-target scope.

Removes the stale Call this first instruction and aligns discovery with context-first guidance. Capability retrieval still reports granted tools, schemas and limits without granting effects or establishing answer evidence by itself.

Successful visible steps may include only a registered skill identifier. The updated form guide documents independent header colors; reading a guide still grants no additional authoring, disclosure or source authority.

Context now exposes independent table header colors and permitted items style keys. Retained UI steps remain excluded from subsequent conversation context, while existing semantic and disclosure boundaries remain in place.

Accepts the expanded typed table-style patch through the existing private draft and records a bounded visible operation count. Scope, binding and final-design checks remain; successful edits still invalidate prior inspection evidence.

The changed tool and guide closure adds presentation history without replacing inspection. Finish still requires the latest ready receipt for the exact candidate, including any new header-color edits.

The changed tool and guide closure retains one-run disclosure authority and evidence invalidation. A visible completed step is presentation only and cannot authorize semantic disclosure or replace final draft inspection.

Retains the changed shared closure while preserving latest-observation, page-index, crop and separate pixel-authorization requirements. Persisted step labels contain no page payload and are excluded from later model history.

The changed shared closure adds retained presentation steps without changing synthetic scenario authority. Scenario diagnostics still do not establish the exact-final inspection required for proposal completion.

The changed shared closure retains visible undo activity without making it commit authority. A successful private undo still invalidates observation and inspection evidence and clears the source handoff.

The changed shared closure preserves bounded replacement notes within a run. Persisted step labels are separate presentation data and do not persist note contents into subsequent model conversation context.

Completed tool steps are attached to the assistant message without replacing proposal evidence. Finish still requires current ready inspection and, for coding grants, current imported artifact lineage; source proposals remain manually applied.

Answer cards retain bounded tool steps separately from the exact answer text. Subsequent provider history includes only permitted message text, while existing answer-evidence and latest-receipt checks remain.

The changed shared tool closure preserves bounded assistant-reported blockers without proposal delivery. Error cards may retain completed steps, but those steps neither verify the blocker nor authorize applying a draft.

The changed shared registry and tool wrapper add presentation history without expanding source access. Listing still requires genuine run-owned workspace authorization and does not grant host filesystem or automatic application authority.

The changed shared closure preserves bounded authorized source reads and untrusted-content treatment. Retained step labels are not source contents and do not grant business-value disclosure or persist workspace files.

The changed shared closure leaves source-search bounds and workspace authorization intact. Visible history grants no additional search paths, draft effects, disclosure permission or committed-state authority.

The changed shared closure does not alter exact-digest writes or null-digest creation semantics. Source writes remain confined to the authorized workspace and never directly apply changes to the live form.

The changed shared closure retains atomic source patch semantics, digest checks and separate creation and deletion rules. Step persistence does not grant source approval or bypass explicit human application.

The changed shared closure adds presentation history without expanding command authority. The schema and guide retain isolated network-denied execution, bounded commands and root cwd semantics. Runtime execution is UNVERIFIED.

The changed shared closure preserves bounded source diff reads against the original fictional starter. A retained successful step is not artifact acceptance, source approval or permission to auto-apply source-derived edits.

The changed shared closure retains successful-current-command artifact retrieval and host-bound opaque descriptors. Persisted activity labels do not replace artifact identity, current lineage or separate import checks.

The expanded table-style schema is available through the same verified artifact-to-draft path. Import still uses scope and binding guards, invalidates inspection, and remains subject to current source lineage and explicit human application.

The guide now documents independent row, header-background and header-text colors with six-digit hex or null reset. Items-only whole-table scope, separate accent styling, final inspection and commit boundaries remain explicit.

Retains the post-baseline workflow-guide update through the changed shared knowledge loader. Workflow groups remain informational human paths or unavailable capabilities, not new callable tools or execution authority.

Retains the post-baseline guide update and changed shared styling closure. Additional tables remain excluded from set_table_style; independent bindings, exact barcodes, source facts and human import and sharing boundaries remain documented.

The shared knowledge and panel lifecycle closure now retains bounded presentation steps without persisting source files or granting effects. Source consent, current artifact lineage, exact inspection and explicit human application remain required.
